title: Contingent Corporate Bill-Audit & Tax-Credit Recovery
uncertainty_note: Editorial sensitivity band, not a statistical interval. Confidence is a supplied classification; independent source review is required.

score_rationale.profit_margin_potential: Profit Margin Potential: 24/25. No-savings-no-fee API parcel refund audits, 36-month commercial utility/waste/CAM overcharge recoveries, property-tax appeals, and WOTC/179D tax-credit splits convert CFO inertia into high-margin recurring contingency checks.

economics.owner_net_profit_potential: $33,000–$504,000 USD annually, before personal taxes and reinvestment
economics.includes_contractors_note: Headcount includes the working owner and recurring contractors as people, not FTE equivalents. Contractors may be part-time. Scaled scenario adds one employee and one contractor; external vendor workforces are not counted as internal team members.
economics.revenue_basis: Earned contingency refund shares, 36-month shared-savings splits, and WOTC processing fees; excludes underlying client utility, freight, or tax bills
economics.cost_basis: Annual net margins include operating expenses and non-owner labor; monthly opex is fixed/semi-fixed overhead only. No owner salary is deducted. Capital needs may grow beyond startup range.
economics.estimate_status: Illustrative assumptions; not verified earnings data

conservative.assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.

base_case.assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.

scaled_small_team.assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.

key_risks: Slow municipal or utility refund issuance
regulatory_notes: Observe Treasury Circular 230 §10.27 contingent-fee rules on federal tax returns, state property-tax consultant licensing, and carrier API terms.
Secure signed Letters of Authorization and baseline invoice snapshots before disclosing tariff or refund findings.

inputs: Customer authorization, carrier account access through approved interfaces, invoice line items, tracking events, package dimensions and weights, and payment or credit records.
Effective carrier contracts, tariff versions, negotiated dimensional divisors, minimum-net-charge provisions, service-guarantee exclusions and claim deadlines by service and geography.
Contingency agreement specifying a 35%–50% fee on realized recoveries, treatment of existing customer disputes, and a separate methodology for compensation on negotiated prospective savings.
plays.mechanism: Audit authorized FedEx Billing Online, UPS Billing Center and DHL invoice exports against shipment events, measured dimensions and the customer's effective service agreements. Recover eligible late-delivery guarantee, dimensional-weight and duplicate-billing overcharges for a negotiated 35%–50% of realized refunds, excluding suspended guarantees, waived rights and expired claims. Separately negotiate minimum-net-charge caps or floors where the carrier offers them, measuring prospective savings against an agreed shipment-level baseline rather than treating a valid contractual minimum as an overcharge.
metrics: Realized refund yield: verified carrier credits or cash received divided by audited parcel spend, segmented by late delivery, dimensional weight and duplicate billing.
Claims acceptance and timeliness: accepted dollars divided by submitted dollars, with the percentage of eligible claims filed before the applicable deadline.
Operator contribution: collected contingency fees minus data, submission and dispute costs; report prospective minimum-charge savings separately from refunds.
plays.name: Parcel Carrier Late-Delivery, Dim-Weight and Minimum-Net-Charge Recovery Operator

platform_risks.detection_metric: Weekly rejection dollars by reason, missed-deadline count, authentication failures and credit-posting latency relative to the carrier-specific baseline.
platform_risks.failure_mode: The carrier rejects claims or restricts access because guarantee eligibility, filing rules or supported integration methods differ from the audit assumptions.
platform_risks.fallback: Pause the affected automation, use authorized exports and supported manual submission channels, and restrict recovery forecasts to confirmed eligible services and open filing windows.
platform_risks.impact: Expected recoveries disappear, processing costs rise and unsupported automation can jeopardize customer account access.
platform_risks.trigger: A guarantee suspension, contractual waiver, claim-window change, undocumented endpoint dependency or portal authentication change.

workflow: 1. Import customer-authorized exports or documented APIs, normalize tracking and invoice identifiers, and create a deadline queue without assuming every carrier provides a claims-submission API.

2. Recalculate eligible charges and delivery commitments using the applicable contract version; remove guarantee suspensions, customer-caused exceptions, duplicates already credited and claims outside their filing window.
3. Submit evidence-backed claims through permitted carrier channels, track acknowledgments and appeals, and present minimum-net-charge negotiation scenarios separately from historical billing errors.
4. Reconcile posted credits to invoices and customer receipts, invoice the agreed contingency only on realized recovery, and monitor negotiated pricing against the agreed baseline.

inputs: Up to 36 months of utility bills, interval-demand data, meter maps, cooling-tower water balances or approved submeters, waste invoices, commercial leases and CAM reconciliations.
Effective utility tariffs, demand-ratchet schedules, sewer-credit rules, manufacturing exemption requirements, waste escalation terms, CAM exclusions and contractual audit deadlines.

Customer authorization and a recovery agreement specifying refund contingencies, prospective shared-savings duration, weather and occupancy adjustments, and supporting engineering or tax-specialist responsibilities.
plays.mechanism: Review up to 36 months of commercial electric, water/sewer, waste and lease CAM charges, subject to each tariff's, contract's and jurisdiction's recovery limits. Test demand-ratchet application, cooling-tower evaporation sewer credits, qualifying manufacturing-meter tax exemptions, waste-hauler escalation clauses and lease-specific CAM allocations against documented eligibility. Charge a negotiated 35%–50% of realized refunds and a separately defined share of verified prospective savings, avoiding double charging the same benefit.
metrics: Realized recovery by category and site: collected refunds or usable credits divided by audited utility, waste and CAM spend.
Verified recurring savings: adjusted baseline charges minus actual post-change charges, controlling for tariff movements, usage, weather, occupancy and service scope.
Recovery efficiency: investigation cost per recovered dollar, median days to credit and percentage of claimed amounts supported by accepted documentation.
plays.name: Commercial Utility, Waste and CAM Historical Recovery Operator

platform_risks.detection_metric: Percentage of proposed recovery dollars lacking required evidence, denial rate by rule and incidence of post-adjustment reversals.
platform_risks.failure_mode: A utility, hauler or landlord denies recovery because the claimed classification or credit lacks contemporaneous eligibility evidence.
platform_risks.fallback: Withdraw unsupported items, pursue documented disputes within surviving deadlines, and implement properly documented prospective metering or classification changes where economically justified.
platform_risks.impact: Historical refunds are reduced or eliminated, and an unsupported prospective adjustment can generate later rebilling.
platform_risks.trigger: Missing cooling-tower metering, an expired lease audit period, unavailable historical tariffs or a manufacturing exemption that does not apply to the billed meter.

workflow: 1. Build a site-and-meter ledger covering the requested 36-month period, identify shorter recovery windows, and preserve timely utility disputes and lease audit notices.

2. Recalculate demand ratchets, eligible evaporation deductions, qualifying manufacturing exemptions, waste increases and CAM allocations using actual tariff and lease provisions rather than assumed universal credits.

3. Submit supported correction requests to utilities, haulers and landlords; obtain required meter verification or exemption documentation and distinguish refundable errors from prospective tariff changes.
4. Reconcile cash refunds and posted credits, establish adjusted post-change baselines, and invoice the 35%–50% recovery fee plus any non-overlapping, contractually defined shared savings.

plays.name: Private B2B Group Purchasing Organization (GPO) Umbrella & Contingent Spend-Audit Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Pool 10,000–75,000+ seats and indirect corporate spend across hundreds of SMB member companies under authorized master GPO volume brackets through Una, OMNIA or private vertical SaaS, parcel and telecom GPOs. Pair negotiated brackets with quarter-end vendor price-floor benchmarking informed by Vendr/Tropic playbooks, targeting 3%–12% vendor-paid administrative rebates and 25%–35% contingent Year-1 shared-savings splits under no savings, no fee agreements. Eligibility, rebate bases and benchmark access must be verified; disclose dual compensation and avoid double-counting rebates in client savings.
inputs: Executed GPO member and supplier agreements defining eligible aggregated spend, volume brackets, administrative rebates and compensation disclosures
Member-authorized invoices and seat inventories plus lawfully obtained, like-for-like Vendr/Tropic-style pricing benchmarks
Contingent audit contracts defining the Year-1 savings baseline, exclusions, 25%–35% fee schedule and independent reconciliation rights
workflow: 1. Enroll eligible SMB members with written authority and aggregate verified seat demand and indirect spend without exchanging competitively sensitive data.
2. Validate GPO purchasing eligibility and negotiate supplier volume brackets using lawful quarter-end benchmarks for comparable service and commitment terms.
3. Present disclosed vendor rebates and contingent fees, secure member approval and implement authorized contract changes against an agreed savings baseline.
4. Reconcile actual Year-1 savings and vendor rebates, charge only earned shared-savings fees and audit bracket eligibility and renewal pricing.
metrics: Verified eligible seats and annual member spend within contracted GPO brackets
Realized Year-1 member savings net of contingent fees on a normalized baseline
Collected administrative rebates and shared-savings fees net of reversals

platform_risks.failure_mode: Ineligible pooled spend or disputed savings invalidates rebates and contingent fees
platform_risks.trigger: Supplier audit, volume-bracket shortfall, undisclosed dual compensation or an unsupported baseline adjustment
platform_risks.impact: Rebate clawbacks, member fee disputes and loss of supplier access
platform_risks.detection_metric: Unsupported eligible spend and disputed savings or rebates as a percentage of billed compensation
platform_risks.fallback: Suspend disputed fees, reconcile documented baselines with members and suppliers, refund unearned amounts and move affected members to eligible purchasing agreements

plays.name: Automated Parcel, LTL Freight & Tariff Overcharge Contingency Auditing
plays.mechanism: Ingest mid-market shippers' UPS/FedEx/LTL EDI billing feeds and CBP Form 7501 customs entry summaries via read-only API to programmatically flag late-delivery SLA refunds, dimensional-weight billing errors, and duty-drawback refunds on a 35–50% contingency split.
inputs: Read-only UPS/FedEx/LTL carrier billing API & EDI 210 feeds
CBP ACE Form 7501 customs entry & HTS tariff schedules
Automated carrier dispute & duty-drawback claim submission engine
workflow: Connect read-only to shipper parcel/freight portals and ingest historical and daily invoice line items
Flag guaranteed-service late deliveries, duplicate accessorial fees, residential surcharges, and eligible export duty drawbacks
Auto-file carrier credit disputes and customs drawback claims, billing the client strictly 35–50% of verified credits posted to their statement
metrics: Recovered credits as % of total annual parcel/freight spend (2–8% target)
Dispute acceptance rate by carrier/customs (%)
Monthly recurring contingency revenue per shipper account

platform_risks.failure_mode: Carrier anti-automation lockouts or GSR (Guaranteed Service Refund) waiver clauses
platform_risks.trigger: Carriers inserting GSR waiver riders into custom shipper pricing agreements or throttling automated dispute bots
platform_risks.impact: Reduction in late-delivery refund volume on waived accounts
platform_risks.detection_metric: Claim approval ratio per carrier and % of audit recovery derived from billing/dim-weight errors vs. GSR
platform_risks.fallback: Pivot audit rules toward non-waivable dimensional-weight, duplicate-charge, LTL freight class, and contract-rate benchmarking recoveries

plays.name: Automated Commercial/Residential Property-Tax Appeal Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Ingest county tax-assessor valuation rolls upon annual notice release, run an automated valuation model (AVM) flagging parcels assessed above comparable neighbor equity ratios, and file bulk administrative tax protests for 30–50% of the first year's verified tax reduction.
inputs: Annual county tax-assessor preliminary valuation rolls & parcel GIS characteristics
Equity-ratio & recent-sale comparable AVM engine
Bulk administrative ARB (Appraisal Review Board) protest filing & hearing pipeline
workflow: Ingest county assessment rolls the day annual valuation notices drop and compute each parcel's assessed-per-sqft percentile against direct neighborhood peers
Mail personalized pre-filled protest postcards showing the owner's exact estimated over-assessment and a QR code to sign a zero-upfront-cost contingency authorization
Auto-generate uniform comparable-equity evidence packets, file bulk administrative protests before the county bar date, and collect 30–50% of Year-1 tax savings
metrics: Protest-window mail-to-signed-authorization conversion %
Percentage of appealed parcels receiving an assessment reduction (65–85% target)
Average net contingency fee per residential ($150–$450) and commercial ($2,000–$15,000) parcel

platform_risks.failure_mode: State property-tax consultant licensing requirements or missed county protest bar dates
platform_risks.trigger: Representing property owners for a fee without required state registration (e.g., Texas TDLR Property Tax Consultant license) or missing the 30/45-day county filing deadline
platform_risks.impact: Rejected bulk filings, administrative fines, or zero contingency revenue for the tax year
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% licensed tax-agent sign-off in regulated states and T-minus-7-day bulk filing completion
platform_risks.fallback: Partner with licensed local property-tax consultants/attorneys of record in regulated states and automate pre-deadline batch electronic filing

plays.name: Automated Form 8850 WOTC (Work Opportunity Tax Credit) & Section 41 R&D Contingency Engine
plays.mechanism: Automate employer-authorized WOTC screening and separately substantiate Section 41 research credits, earning outcome-linked service fees only where permitted; program authorization, qualifying activities, wage coordination, and professional fee restrictions govern each claim.
inputs: Consented hiring records, Form 8850 responses, and payroll hours
Research project evidence and qualified expense ledgers
State workforce certification procedures and tax-year credit and fee rules
workflow: 1. Confirm WOTC authorization for each hire date and complete required prescreening by the job-offer date
2. Submit Form 8850 and required supporting forms within the applicable 28-day deadline and track state certification and qualifying hours
3. Separately document Section 41 qualifying research and expenses, reconciling wage overlap and applicable deduction adjustments with a tax professional
4. Obtain employer and preparer approval before filing, retain audit support, and collect permitted fees without guaranteeing credits
metrics: Timely WOTC certification submission rate
Substantiated credits realized by the employer
Net permitted service fees after review and filing costs

platform_risks.failure_mode: Credit denial or impermissible contingent-fee arrangement
platform_risks.trigger: Expired program authority, late certification, unsupported research expenses, or restricted practitioner compensation
platform_risks.impact: Reduced credits, amended returns, penalties, and fee repayment exposure
platform_risks.detection_metric: Deadline exceptions, certification denials, and unsupported expense share
platform_risks.fallback: Exclude unsupported claims and use compliant fixed-fee payroll and research-documentation services under independent tax review

plays.name: IRC Section 179D Government & Nonprofit Energy-Deduction Allocation Brokering
plays.mechanism: Coordinate eligible government and tax-exempt building owners, qualifying designers, and independent energy certifiers to document Section 179D deduction allocations; compensation is for permitted services, not resale of a freely transferable deduction.
inputs: Public and nonprofit building project records and construction dates
Designer contracts and owner allocation authority
Independent energy certification and applicable tax-year eligibility rules
workflow: 1. Screen building projects for eligible ownership, construction timing, and current Section 179D availability
2. Verify qualifying designer work, energy certification, deduction limits, and applicable wage and apprenticeship requirements
3. Obtain authorized owner allocation letters and reconcile prior allocations to prevent duplicate deductions
4. Deliver the substantiated file to the designer's tax adviser and collect disclosed legally permitted coordination fees
metrics: Certified eligible deduction value allocated
Owner-approved allocation conversion rate
Net coordination fees after certification and review costs

platform_risks.failure_mode: Deduction allocation rejected or reduced
platform_risks.trigger: Ineligible project dates, unsupported designer status, deficient certification, or duplicate allocation
platform_risks.impact: Lost tax benefit, assessment exposure, and disputed service fees
platform_risks.detection_metric: Unresolved eligibility and allocation exceptions per project
platform_risks.fallback: Pause allocation, obtain independent tax review, and offer fixed-fee documentation support only for eligible projects

plays.name: Transferable Federal & State Tax Credit Brokerage & Syndication (IRA § 6418 / Film / Historic)
plays.mechanism: Scraping federal DOE/EPA interconnection queues, state film offices, and historic-preservation registries to originate transferable tax credits (IRC § 6418 Clean Energy Investment/Production Credits, Georgia/Louisiana Film Credits, State Historic Rehab & Brownfield Credits) from cash-strapped project developers at $0.82–$0.88 on the dollar and flipping them in simultaneous escrow closings to corporate and HNW taxpayers at $0.92–$0.96 on the dollar.
inputs: State film-office production certifications, National Park Service Part 2/3 Historic Preservation filings, and utility solar/biogas/storage interconnection queues
IRS Energy Credits Online pre-filing registration verification and tax-credit recapture insurance underwriting partners
Outbound network of CPA managing partners, corporate tax directors, and family-office CIOs with $1M–$50M+ in quarterly federal/state tax liabilities
workflow: Monitor public project registries to identify middle-market solar, RNG, battery storage, independent film, and historic-rehab developers holding $1M–$25M in newly generated transferable credits
Lock up exclusive purchase or placement options at $0.83–$0.89 per $1.00 of credit prior to quarterly corporate estimated tax deadlines (April 15, June 15, Sept 15, Dec 15)
Package the credits with a third-party CPA cost-segregation/eligibility opinion and tax-credit recapture insurance policy

Execute a simultaneous bilateral escrow closing with a corporate taxpayer at $0.92–$0.95 on the dollar—saving the buyer 5–8% guaranteed on their tax bill while capturing a 400–800 bps riskless spread ($40k–$80k per $1M block)
metrics: Face value of tax credits placed per quarter ($5M–$100M+)
Net retained principal/brokerage spread (400–800 bps) per closed tranche
Days in escrow from developer IRS registration number issuance to wire settlement

platform_risks.failure_mode: IRS § 6418 recapture event or state department-of-revenue basis challenge
platform_risks.trigger: Project developer inflating eligible cost basis or taking a clean-energy asset out of service during the 5-year recapture window
platform_risks.impact: Taxpayer recapture assessment plus penalties if uninsured
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% independent Big-4/national CPA cost-basis audit and mandatory A-rated tax-credit recapture insurance binder on every tranche
platform_risks.fallback: Never take unhedged balance-sheet inventory risk; close strictly via simultaneous back-to-back escrow funded by the buyer's wire and backed by non-cancelable tax-credit insurance

plays.name: State Film, Historic Rehabilitation (HTC) & Brownfield Transferable Tax Credit Placement
plays.mechanism: Match certified state film, historic rehabilitation, and brownfield credits with eligible taxpayers at negotiated discounts, retaining disclosed placement fees; transferability and buyer usability are state-specific and do not imply federal historic credits can be sold outright.
inputs: State agency project approvals and issued credit certificates
Transfer rules, recapture terms, and seller ownership records
Buyer state tax liabilities and escrow placement agreements
workflow: 1. Identify certified credits and verify state-specific transferability, issuance status, and remaining carryforward life
2. Have independent advisers validate eligible costs, ownership, liens, recapture exposure, and buyer utilization limits
3. Match approved buyers and sellers with disclosed pricing, fees, indemnities, and any available insurance exclusions
4. Complete required agency transfer approvals and escrow settlement, then retain filing and post-close monitoring records
metrics: Certified transferable credit face value placed
Net placement fee per settled transaction
Transfer approval and escrow cycle days

platform_risks.failure_mode: Transfer rejected or purchased credit unusable
platform_risks.trigger: State rule change, certificate defect, recapture event, or buyer liability mismatch
platform_risks.impact: Failed closing or buyer tax shortfall and indemnity dispute
platform_risks.detection_metric: Unresolved certificate exceptions and buyer utilization coverage
platform_risks.fallback: Suspend settlement under diligence contingencies and rematch only verified eligible credits without guaranteeing tax savings

plays.name: B2B Class-Action & Antitrust Settlement Contingency Recovery
plays.mechanism: Monitor multibillion-dollar corporate antitrust and commercial class-action settlement funds (payment-card interchange, freight, auto parts, commercial insurance, SaaS) where 85–90% of eligible small businesses never file, and recover verified payouts on a 25–33% contingency fee.
inputs: Active federal B2B class-action settlement docket calendar & claims-administrator portals
B2B merchant-processing, fleet, & vendor spend intake pipeline
Contingency claim-preparation & court-authorized third-party filing agreements
workflow: Track open and upcoming commercial class-action settlements with verified court-appointed claims administrators and $50M–$5B+ settlement pools
Sign zero-upfront-cost (25–33% contingency) authorization agreements with operating restaurants, medical practices, retailers, and fleets
Extract historical merchant statements or vendor invoices, submit audited claim packages to the settlement administrator, and reconcile fee splits upon disbursement
metrics: Average gross settlement recovery per enrolled business ($5,000–$150,000+)
Claim acceptance rate by court-appointed administrator (%)
Net contingency fee per operator hour invested

platform_risks.failure_mode: Claim rejection, administrator audit hold, or court cap on third-party filer fees
platform_risks.trigger: Submitting unsubstantiated spend estimates, missing court bar dates, or failing to include required third-party filer disclosures
platform_risks.impact: Delayed payout disbursement or court-mandated fee reduction
platform_risks.detection_metric: Deficiency-notice rate (<2% target) and 100% court-approved disclosure compliance
platform_risks.fallback: File strictly for verified operating businesses with primary processor/vendor statements and use court-approved third-party claim-filing riders

plays.name: Subsidized / Developer-Tenant Multi-Inbox Cold Outbound Infrastructure
plays.mechanism: Provisioning hundreds of isolated secondary domains across subsidized Microsoft 365 developer/partner tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing, and low-cost SMTP relays—sending strictly 15–25 plain-text emails per inbox per day across 300+ free/subsidized mailboxes to deliver 150,000+ monthly B2B cold emails into primary inboxes without paying $6–$12/seat retail Google Workspace pricing.
inputs: Lookalike secondary domain portfolio with automated SPF, DKIM (2048-bit), DMARC (`p=quarantine`/`reject`), and custom tracking-free MX records
Subsidized M365 partner/developer tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing catch-alls, and distributed SMTP sending nodes
Automated peer-to-peer warmup network and master unibox reply-routing webhook
workflow: Provision 100–300 secondary sending domains and bind 2–3 mailboxes per domain via automated DNS and tenant scripts
Warm every mailbox for 14–21 days with realistic thread-depth conversations before introducing live outbound prospects
Cap daily outbound volume at <=20 zero-link, zero-tracking-pixel plain-text messages per mailbox per day to stay completely beneath ESP volume heuristics
Aggregate all prospect replies into a single unified AI-triaged inbox that books qualified B2B sales calls on pay-per-show or retainer terms
metrics: Primary-inbox placement rate (%) across Gmail and Microsoft 365 seed tests
All-in monthly infrastructure cost per 10,000 delivered plain-text emails ($)
Positive reply rate (%) and booked meetings per 1,000 prospects contacted

platform_risks.failure_mode: Tenant-wide outbound throttling or domain-footprint blacklisting (Spamhaus DBL)
platform_risks.trigger: Placing too many domains inside a single tenant, embedding tracking pixels, or exceeding 30 sends/day per mailbox
platform_risks.impact: Tenant suspension or domain-level spam-folder routing
platform_risks.detection_metric: Daily seed-list inbox placement (%) and bounce rate (<1.5% hard threshold)
platform_risks.fallback: Enforce max 2–3 domains per tenant, strip all open/click tracking pixels, verify 100% of leads via SMTP catch-all checks before sending, and keep hot-standby warmed domains ready for instant swap

plays.name: High-Velocity DM Outbound & Trigger Funnels
plays.mechanism: Replace blind cold mass-DM blasts (which die to PeerFloodError and silent Message Request graveyards) with high-velocity comment-to-DM triggers, hand-raiser reaction hooks, and multi-inbox warm signal routing.
inputs: Short-form / community trigger posts ('Comment KEYWORD')
Signal-verified prospect handles
Automated DM qualification & booking bridge
workflow: Publish high-curiosity teardown or resource posts where prospects comment a trigger keyword or react to unlock a playbook or calculator
Deliver instant automated DM replies to warm hand-raisers (bypassing cold-DM filters because the user initiated interaction) or send contextual 1-to-1 DMs referencing an active public request
Qualify budget and timeline inside a 3-message DM micro-funnel and transition immediately to a booked call, checkout link, or owned SMS/email list
metrics: Trigger-comment to DM delivery rate
DM reply-to-qualified-conversation %
Revenue per 100 DM threads

platform_risks.failure_mode: PeerFloodError, shadow-filtering into 'Hidden Requests', or link-domain blacklisting
platform_risks.trigger: Sending identical unsolicited cold DMs with raw external URLs across freshly registered or SIM-farmed accounts
platform_risks.impact: Near-0% inbox placement, outbound DM block, or permanent account suspension
platform_risks.detection_metric: Seen/reply ratio below 10% and outbound PeerFloodError / action-block frequency
platform_risks.fallback: Require user-initiated trigger action (comment/reaction/inbound message) before automated DM dispatch and send external links only after the prospect replies
